text: When hash-based ordering or shuffling must be reproducible, control the hash source: set `PYTHONHASHSEED` explicitly in tests that assert on hash-dependent ordering, and avoid Python's built-in `hash()` on strings when consistency is needed across processes or Python versions; use a stable `hashlib` algorithm instead.
reason: Python's built-in `hash()` is salted per process and implementation-dependent, which makes ordering flaky; both explicit seed pinning in tests and stable hashing in implementation address the same reproducibility requirement.
scope: hash-ordering-dependent tests and cross-process/version-stable ordering logic
common_pattern: Hash-based ordering must be made deterministic by controlling or replacing Python's salted built-in hash behavior.

text: In tests, whenever a value is hardcoded, uses a magic offset, or is derived from a non-obvious assumption (e.g., `last().id + 100`, `pk=1`, a pre-signed token or serialized fixture), add an inline comment explaining why that exact value is needed, how it was produced, and what incorrect behavior it is meant to catch.
reason: Prevents future maintainers from removing, altering, or 'simplifying' the value without understanding its role, which would silently destroy the test's coverage and readability.
common_pattern: All three generalizations require an explanatory comment whenever a test setup contains a magic, hardcoded, or computed-from-a-non-obvious-assumption value, so future maintainers understand the value's purpose and do not remove or 'simplify' it.

text: Do not use text/blob field types (`TextField`, `NCLOB`, etc.) in lookups or tests that generate SQL `IN()` clauses; choose a scalar type (character, integer, date). Some backends (Oracle) disallow blob/clob columns inside `IN()`.
reason: Such queries crash on backends that forbid blob/clob in `IN()`, producing failures with no added coverage value.
common_pattern: When writing backend-specific database code, branches on column/field types must account for every field type that maps to the same underlying backend storage type (and, conversely, tests/queries must avoid field types the backend disallows in certain constructs like IN()). Groups 1/3/4/2 cover the 'cover all equivalent field types' half; 6/7/8 cover 'enumerate exhaustively / reuse a shared constant'; 5 is the anti-pattern consequence.

text: When porting or backporting code from an upstream or canonical implementation (an upstream PR/branch, CPython stdlib, or another project's utility), also port the corresponding upstream test cases to the project's test suite to verify behavioral parity and branch coverage. Skip tests that duplicate existing coverage or add little value.
reason: Upstream tests already cover subtle edge cases and semantics; carrying them forward ensures parity and licenses simplification of defensive code, while pruning redundant tests avoids test bloat.
common_pattern: When porting/backporting code (features, functions, utilities) from an upstream or canonical source (prior PR, upstream PR, CPython stdlib), transitively port the corresponding upstream tests to verify parity and coverage — but skip tests that are redundant with existing coverage or add little value.

text: Add migration writer/serializer tests as unit tests in the existing tests/migrations/test_writer.py `WriterTests` class rather than creating a new test module or migration integration tests; defer any test-module reorganization to a separate refactor commit.
reason: Keeps migration serialization tests consolidated with shared helpers/assertions, matches the established organization of this module, and avoids splitting closely related tests without a deliberate refactor.
common_pattern: Conventions for Django migration writer/serializer tests: place tests in the established test module/class and express assertions through the provided helper with readable expected values.

text: When testing `MigrationExecutor` logging in `tests/migrations/test_executor.py`, cover every relevant combination of operation variant (apply/unapply), execution mode (real/fake), and log level; consolidate analogous combinations into a single test using `subTest` where practical.
reason: Logging behavior can differ between apply and unapply paths and between real and fake execution modes, so missing any combination leaves an untested path that may regress unnoticed.
common_pattern: Migration executor logging tests should cover all symmetric combinations of operation variant (apply/unapply) and execution mode (real/fake), using subTest to consolidate analogous cases.

text: In test helpers that format assertion arguments, pass values through the helper's parameter list instead of interpolating them inline with `.format()` on string literals, and guard any formatter call (e.g. `black.format_str`) so unparseable input falls back to the original value rather than raising a parse error.
reason: The helper should own escaping/quoting consistently, and formatters raise on non-Python content (e.g. `<&>`), which would make an otherwise valid assertion fail unpredictably.
common_pattern: Both generalizations concern how test assertion helpers handle string formatting/substitution: callers should delegate value substitution to the helper's parameter list rather than interpolating inline, and any formatter applied inside the helper must be defensive so unparseable input does not raise.

text: When a test generates a temporary Python settings file/module by serializing settings values (e.g. via `repr()`), serialize only settings whose representation is a standalone valid literal; if non-literal values must be included, also emit the required imports so the generated file remains self-contained.
reason: `repr()` of arbitrary objects can produce expressions that depend on external imports or trigger import-time side effects, making generated test settings brittle across backends and configurations.
scope: Tests that synthesize temporary settings modules, especially `tests/migrations/test_loader.py` and similar test helpers.
common_pattern: Tests that synthesize temporary Python settings modules by serializing settings values must avoid emitting `repr()` output for non-literal objects, because that output can require imports not present in the generated file and fail with `NameError` or import-time side effects.

text: When a test depends on SQL NUMERIC decimal precision normalization (for example, `Decimal("8")` round-tripping as `Decimal("8.000")`), skip it on MongoDB instead of adding backend conversion logic such as `quantize()` solely to make the test pass. Specifically, `test_roundtrip_integer_with_trailing_zeros` should be skipped on MongoDB.
reason: MongoDB does not automatically pad decimal precision like SQL NUMERIC types do. Emulating this in backend conversion code adds runtime overhead and implements SQL-specific behavior rather than actual MongoDB-to-Python conversion.
common_pattern: Backend-specific decimal precision differences (SQL NUMERIC vs MongoDB) should be handled by skipping the affected test on MongoDB, not by adding production quantization logic that only emulates SQL semantics.

text: Gate manager inclusion in migration state and related tests on whether a manager has `use_in_migrations = True`, not on a hard-coded manager attribute name such as `objects`. Tests should cover non-default manager names (e.g. `blub`) as well as `objects`.
reason: Manager names are arbitrary and user-definable, so they do not reliably indicate migration participation or expected migration-state behavior.
scope: Django migration-state manager serialization and tests
common_pattern: Django migration and migration-state code must consistently rely on historical model state and semantic migration flags (`apps.get_model`, `use_in_migrations`) instead of global/current model classes or incidental manager names like `objects`.

text: When modifying request body parsing, wrap parse failures in explicit error handling and add regression tests covering the changed behavior, parse-failure paths, and edge cases such as missing headers, empty bodies, and header precedence. Place request-body regression tests in tests/requests_tests/tests.py when applicable.
reason: Malformed input should fail predictably rather than surfacing as an unhandled error, and tests lock down the fixed behavior while preserving coverage for edge cases that are easy to regress.
common_pattern: Request body parsing changes require both robust error handling and regression tests covering parse failures and edge cases.

text: When SQL-generation logic loops over or branches on a computed number of columns (e.g., `num_cols = len(rhs.select) + len(rhs.annotation_select)`), add tests covering the multi-column case (`num_cols > 1`) in addition to the single-column case.
reason: Multi-column branches can generate different SQL/parameter structures and would otherwise be untested; this ensures the loop and column aliasing work for more than one column.
common_pattern: Correctly handling multi-column / composite (ColPairs) selections in SQL generation: counting the expanded column set rather than the raw select-list length, using the single canonical column-count attribute, and adding tests that exercise more than one column.

text: When an API supports a context-manager mode that does not accept keyword arguments, add tests that pass those keyword arguments inside the `with` statement; if a keyword argument is unsupported in context-manager usage, assert the resulting exception and its message.
reason: Context-manager code paths can silently ignore keyword arguments or raise separate errors; explicit tests close coverage gaps and prevent divergence between direct-call and context-manager usage.
common_pattern: Handling of unexpected keyword arguments in constructor/method APIs: surface them with explicit, consistent errors rather than silently ignoring or over-broadly catching, and cover the context-manager code path with tests.

text: When running migration checks or tests, enable all optional app variants (e.g., `gis_enabled=True`) so that backend-specific apps' migrations are exercised.
reason: Excluding optional app sets hides pending migrations for those apps, causing the check to report success while real missing migrations exist.
common_pattern: Defensive handling of optional settings, attributes, and app variants in Django migration code.

text: Test fakes that subclass production classes must not forward caller-supplied real-resource parameters (e.g., host/connection arguments) to the real superclass; accept them with **kwargs, override with test-safe defaults, and pass those safe defaults to super().__init__ so the fake's behavior is not argument-dependent.
reason: If constructor arguments are forwarded to the real superclass, a caller can accidentally turn the fake into a real connection, making the fake's behavior surprising and dependent on call-site arguments.
common_pattern: Test-double design: test doubles/fakes should conform to production interfaces without forcing production changes, and should be safe, faithful, and inspectable rather than argument-dependent or burdened with redundant test-only state.

text: In test automation and test server utilities, bind to an OS-assigned ephemeral port by using port 0 instead of a hard-coded port. For Django development servers, invoke `manage.py runserver 0`; for test server/thread constructors, default the port argument to 0 when backward compatibility permits.
reason: Avoids port-conflict flakiness when tests run concurrently or when a hard-coded port such as 8001 is already in use, and provides a sensible backward-compatible default for new port parameters.
scope: Test automation shell scripts and test server utilities, including Django runserver commands and test HTTP server/thread constructors.
common_pattern: Use an OS-assigned ephemeral port (port 0) instead of a fixed port in test automation and test server utilities to avoid port conflicts.

text: When code relies on a conversion/coercion helper (e.g. force_text, force_bytes, formfield(), a conditional conversion branch), add tests that exercise the failure or alternative path — construct inputs where the wrong API, a removed conversion call, or an untested non-default argument produces different results — so the test fails if that conversion behavior regresses.
reason: Success-path-only tests let conversion helpers silently regress (dropped coercion calls, wrong API, or unjustified non-default arguments such as strings_only=True) without anyone noticing.
common_pattern: Tests for conversion/coercion helpers must pin down the specific conversion behavior they depend on: cover the failing/alternative branch (not just the happy path) and construct inputs that make the test fail if the intended API or conversion call is removed, swapped, or given unnecessary non-default arguments.

text: When path-handling behavior changes, update the corresponding tests to assert that the security exception (SuspiciousFileOperation with the path-traversal message) is raised for suspicious input, rather than asserting a transformed/sanitized filename, so the validation contract is locked in and regressions are caught.
reason: Tests should encode the error contract for suspicious input, not the incidental value produced by sanitization; this prevents reintroducing redundant normalization and keeps traversal detection covered.
scope: tests for model_fields/file-field filename generation and path handling
common_pattern: Django file/path handling should rely on established path-safety primitives (django.utils._os.safe_join, validate_file_name) that raise an explicit SuspiciousFileOperation for suspicious input, instead of ad hoc silent sanitization (e.g. os.path.basename stripping); correspondingly, regression tests should assert the raised exception rather than the sanitized value. A minority of generalizations argue for sanitizing before/alongside safe_join, creating a partial contradiction that is resolved in favor of the validation-first consensus.

text: Update a test's name whenever its assertions or expected behavior change, so the name accurately describes the condition actually being verified.
reason: Test names act as documentation; stale names mislead readers about the test's purpose and are harder to maintain when assertions are broadened or altered.
common_pattern: Test method names must be updated whenever the assertions or expected behavior they verify change, so the name accurately describes what the test checks.

text: In tests for Django request encoding behavior, cover consecutive encoding changes on cached request data (asserting re-decoding to the latest encoding) and document any known deviations from the documented HttpRequest.encoding semantics with a ticket reference.
reason: Request encoding tests need to verify that cached decoded data updates when encoding changes repeatedly, and that known discrepancies from documented behavior are captured with ticket references for maintainability.
common_pattern: Tests for Django request encoding behavior must account for dynamic encoding state and documented deviations.

text: When modifying formatting or encoding output, maintain comprehensive test coverage across all related implementations: add equivalent tests for parallel formatter modules, verify that all alternative format methods are independently tested before changing the default output, and preserve existing output for simple/common inputs so that existing tests remain valid.
reason: Changes to formatting or encoding can affect multiple code paths and tests. Covering parallel modules, testing alternatives before default changes, and avoiding unnecessary test churn for unchanged behavior all help prevent regressions and keep changes focused.
common_pattern: Testing and output preservation considerations when modifying formatting or encoding behavior

text: For warning/filter matching utilities with optional constraints, only short-circuit an unconstrained filter to a definite match or ignore; if module or line-number constraints are present, require caller/module context instead of guessing, and test both broad (category-only) and narrowed (module + message/line) matching to verify the filtering scope.
reason: Constrained warning filters cannot be evaluated safely without knowing the warning source module and line, and tests must confirm omitted optional filters do not over-filter while provided filters correctly restrict matches.
common_pattern: Warning/filter matching utilities must correctly handle optional narrowing constraints such as module, line, or message: unconstrained filters can be decided directly, while constrained filters require caller/module context, and tests should cover both broad and narrowed matching.

text: When adding tests for a utility with an inverse or mirrored counterpart that shares a code path (e.g., timesince/timeuntil via reversed=True), assert both directions in the same test and match the assertion structure of related sibling tests.
reason: Symmetric assertions protect against accidental divergence of shared code paths, reduce review friction, and ensure consistent coverage across related tests.
common_pattern: Tests for symmetric or inverse utility functions that share a code path should assert both directions and follow the assertion structure of related sibling tests.

text: When adding a `continue`/skip path (or otherwise changing the control flow) in a loop, update the corresponding tests to assert that skipped/invalid items do not produce subsequent processing output.
reason: Tests must cover the changed control flow and user-visible output sequences, otherwise the test suite will no longer match the command's behavior.
common_pattern: In a loop that validates each item, when an item is reported invalid, the success/progress output for that item must be suppressed (via `continue` or an `elif` guard) so users don't see misleading 'processing X' messages, while all items are still evaluated and corresponding tests assert the suppressed output.

text: In view tests, exercise the real request/response lifecycle through the framework test client or existing shared helpers, trigger errors/behavior at the same lifecycle point as production, and keep setup minimal by creating/authenticating users or custom requests only when the code path reads them, reusing shared helpers instead of ad-hoc views, and avoiding test-only emulation of feature internals or manual middleware wiring; test-only error views should be minimal and clearly labeled as test views.
reason: These generalizations all converge on the same principle: view tests should verify actual application behavior with minimal, non-emulating setup. They consistently reject manual request construction, middleware wiring, redundant user/auth setup, ad-hoc helper views, and test-only reimplementations of feature logic.
scope: Django view tests and test helper views
common_pattern: View tests and test-only view helpers should exercise the real request/response lifecycle with minimal, reusable setup, rather than manually wiring lifecycle details or emulating feature internals.

text: In admin test models with soft-delete, represent deletion with an explicit `deleted` boolean field; make the default manager filter on `deleted=False` and expose an unfiltered `all_objects` manager for admin/queryset overrides that need soft-deleted rows; in tests, create explicit active and deleted objects via the flag instead of hardcoded primary keys.
reason: This merges the complementary manager-design and test-usage generalizations into one robust rule for soft-delete test models.
common_pattern: Soft-delete modeling in admin test models using an explicit `deleted` boolean field, a default manager filtered to `deleted=False`, and a separate unfiltered `all_objects` manager for code/tests that must access soft-deleted rows.

text: When a CLI command has an option that selects a backend/routing (e.g. `--using`), test it by asserting the selected backend/alias directly on the resulting object (e.g. `message.sent_using == "notifications"`) instead of generic assertions, and cover the full option surface: the default path when the option is omitted (e.g. `sent_using == "default"`) and each per-recipient mode (e.g. `--admins`, `--managers`) to verify the option is propagated to every helper. Prefer a dedicated default-case test (e.g. `test_using_default()` in `tests/mail/test_sendtestemail.py`).
reason: A test named for a command option should fail if that option is ignored; asserting the selected backend directly gives precise, durable coverage, and per-path plus default tests catch missing option propagation in each branch.
scope: tests (CLI command tests for backend/routing options)
common_pattern: Tests for a CLI option that selects a backend/routing (e.g. `--using` on `sendtestemail`) must assert the option-specific outcome directly on the resulting object and cover both the option-provided and default/omitted paths (including each per-recipient mode), rather than relying on generic assertions.

text: When adding a new branch to display/rendering logic that handles a field's value, add a test covering the case where the value or relation resolves to null/None, locking in the intended fallback behavior.
reason: New conditional branches in display logic often have subtle behavior for empty/null relations; a regression test documents and locks in the intended fallback behavior.
common_pattern: When modifying display/formatting logic to handle a sentinel or edge value, ensure complete coverage: guard every parallel code path and sibling helper, and add tests for unhandled/None values.

text: In browser-based (Selenium) test classes, allocate expensive shared resources once per class in `setupClass` — mapping each configuration (e.g. browser name) to its resource — expose them to individual tests through a `cached_property` (e.g. a `selenium` property that looks up the WebDriver using the per-test `self.browser`), and release them in `tearDownClass` (calling `quit()` on every stored driver). When a class is parameterized across multiple configurations, run all tests for one configuration as a group, starting that configuration's resource before its first test and stopping it after its last test before moving on.
reason: Creating WebDriver per test is expensive, slows the suite, risks leaking browser processes, and interleaving configurations holds multiple heavy resources open at once; class/config-scoped lifecycle keeps resource management sequential and leak-free.
scope: Django Selenium / browser-automation test infrastructure (django/test/selenium.py and similar)
common_pattern: Conventions for constructing Django Selenium/browser-based test classes: how to expose test configuration (browser specs) as class attributes and how to manage the lifecycle of expensive shared resources (WebDriver instances) at class/configuration scope rather than per test.

text: Configure the Django database engine in test settings to the spatial backend for the database under test, e.g. `django.contrib.gis.db.backends.oracle`, when running GIS tests against a spatial database.
reason: GIS tests must execute against the correct spatial database backend rather than the default non-spatial backend.
common_pattern: Django spatial/GIS backends require explicit configuration and robust, environment-aware handling of spatial database backends and native extensions.

text: In browser/E2E tests, prefer the test framework's native APIs for layout measurements, assertions, and interactions over injected or string-evaluated JavaScript that produces the same result.
reason: Keeps test logic in the test language, improving readability and maintainability and avoiding brittle string-based JavaScript evaluation.
common_pattern: Playwright/browser integration test robustness: how to handle browser- and platform-specific behavior, workarounds, and event-dependent regression tests without introducing brittle or misleading tests

text: When adding or changing composite/tuple-key support, add regression tests that cover F() expressions referencing those columns (e.g., F("pk") or F("<composite_alias>__pk")) and assert they resolve to the composite column expression (ColPairs) and compile correctly through joins, rather than being handled as a scalar col.
reason: Direct field access and F() expressions can take different resolution paths for composite keys; without an explicit F()-reference test, join/alias handling can regress to scalar-column behavior during query compilation.
scope: tests for composite-field and tuple-lookup behavior
common_pattern: Add explicit regression tests for F() expressions referencing composite/tuple-key columns, because F() references may resolve differently from direct field references and can silently fall back to scalar column handling instead of composite column expressions such as ColPairs or compile-time join handling.

text: For each documented or supported usage of a new feature (e.g., new expression types, mixed function/column index expressions, enumerated entry points like alias ordering or whole-tuple lookups), add a corresponding test that exercises that specific case—asserting both creation and expression/ordering behavior for index expressions.
reason: Enumerated use cases represent the feature's contract; testing each prevents regressions in any of them and ensures documented behavior actually works.
common_pattern: When introducing or documenting new feature capabilities (expression types, index combinations, usage entry points), add tests covering each documented/enumerated use case.

text: In ORM query-construction/compilation changes and their regression tests, preserve and verify intended SQL semantics: do not silently drop predicate/condition fragments (including constant booleans) to make a crash disappear; reproduce the reported query shape, including relevant relation joins; assert that all original conditions are present in the generated SQL/results; and add comments for non-obvious internal query-compilation assertions.
reason: Tests that only check crash absence or simplified query shapes can pass while the generated SQL is semantically wrong because criteria were dropped. Fixes must preserve condition nodes, and tests must assert the intended join/result semantics.
common_pattern: Regression tests and fixes for ORM query construction/compilation must preserve and assert intended SQL semantics, rather than masking crashes by dropping predicates or simplifying the reported query shape.

text: When expanding resolved test cases with `get_test_variations()` in `load_tests_for_label` (django/test/runner.py), group the test cases by their actual class (`type(test)`) and invoke each group's own `get_test_variations()`. Do not derive the variation list from `test_cases[0]` and apply it to all test cases, because whole-module labels resolve tests from multiple sibling classes and re-applying one class's variations duplicates (or drops) variants.
reason: A label naming a whole module resolves every registered test class in that module. Using the first test's class variations for all resolved tests causes over-counting (e.g., 8 instead of 4) by re-expanding tests that are already variations of a different class, and can drop the intended variants of the other classes.
common_pattern: All four generalizations describe the same bug-fix pattern: when expanding resolved test cases into variations, they must be grouped by each test case's own class (`type(test)`) and expanded with that class's variation hook, rather than deriving variations from `test_cases[0]` and applying them to all test cases. Whole-module labels resolve multiple test classes, so the naive approach duplicates tests.

text: For test support views, prefer flexibility over duplication: parameterize an existing view (e.g., extract `content_type` from `request.GET`) instead of adding a new dedicated view per variant, and discover supported media types using the protocol-standard mechanism (e.g., HEAD per the relevant RFC) rather than hard-coding expected formats.
reason: Keeps the test surface protocol-correct and resilient, reduces duplication of test support views, and makes adding new test cases cheaper.
common_pattern: When writing test-only views/tests, prefer flexible, protocol-aware mechanisms (parameterizing existing views via request.GET, using standards-defined discovery such as HEAD) over duplicating views or hard-coding expectations.

text: When pushing changes that trigger CI builds (e.g., Jenkins), batch related changes into as few pushes as possible rather than pushing many commits in quick succession.
reason: Each push triggers a full CI build; rapid successive pushes waste CI resources and require canceling redundant builds.
common_pattern: Developers must execute the relevant test suite locally before pushing/submitting, rather than relying on CI or reviewers to catch test failures — applied across multiple frameworks (Django runtests.py, npm test) and multiple PRs.

text: When modifying conditional logic that routes specific lookup types or state handling in ORM query/lookup paths, verify that all previously handled lookup types or state adjustments remain covered, and keep compatibility adjustments even if they seem unrelated to the new feature, to avoid regressions in existing tests.
reason: Both generalizations describe the same pitfall: changing a conditional (backend-specific branch or state flag) can silently drop necessary special handling, causing existing tests to regress. The rule merges their complementary concerns—coverage of all original cases and retention of compatibility adjustments—into one actionable guideline for ORM lookup modifications.
common_pattern: When modifying conditional logic that routes specific lookup types or state handling in ORM query/lookup paths, ensure all previously handled cases remain covered and keep compatibility adjustments to prevent regressions in existing tests.

text: When introducing or changing inheritance-aware class-level caches, add regression tests that access the cache through a subclass and assert it retains object identity with the base class value, and that sibling/subclass caches stay properly scoped without leaking parent-class values.
reason: Inheritance-aware caching fails subtly (eviction, contamination across siblings like DateTimeField/DateField), so identity and scoping assertions lock in the expected per-class behavior and guard against future regressions.
common_pattern: Caching values in a class hierarchy must be scoped per-class so that inheritance and subclassing work correctly, rather than relying on descriptor/keyed caches that leak, evict, or share values across classes.

text: When WKB serialization tests fail for edge cases such as empty geometries or varying SRID values, handle the special cases with conditionals in the WKBWriter class rather than changing the test expectation; inspect and reuse existing project commit patterns for similar GEOS serialization fixes.
reason: Tests should specify expected serialization output, while the writer implementation should produce correct output for special geometry/SRID cases. Reusing established project fix patterns keeps the implementation consistent and avoids treating serialization failures as test-only issues.
common_pattern: Implementation-over-test-expectation for GEOS/WKB serialization edge cases: fix the writer class with conditionals rather than changing tests, and align with existing project fix patterns.

text: When testing dry-run SQL capture for the database cache backend, configure the test with a table name that does not already exist. Dry-run mode intercepts SQL after the table-exists check, so reusing an existing table name short-circuits CREATE TABLE and leaves no SQL to assert on. Do not dismiss table-name setup as irrelevant just because dry-run skips side effects—the existence check still runs before interception.
reason: Ensures the dry-run capture test actually exercises and observes CREATE TABLE output instead of silently producing no SQL because the existence check bailed out first.
common_pattern: Dry-run SQL capture tests still depend on code that runs before SQL interception, such as the table-existence check, so table-name setup can be necessary to ensure CREATE TABLE is emitted and observable.

text: When a URL fixture entry is invalid only because of a disallowed substring, repair it by removing the offending substring (checking for and removing all other instances of the same disallowed character/sequence) rather than deleting the test case, so its remaining parsing coverage is preserved.
reason: A URL is only valid if every component is accepted, so a single removal may leave the case still failing; minimally editing instead of deleting retains complex, intended valid-URL coverage.
common_pattern: All generalizations concern how to maintain and extend Django's URL validation test suite: where test cases live (fixture files vs. inline), how to repair broken fixture entries, and how to ensure fixture cases actually exercise the regex features being changed.

text: In test helpers, parameterize the helper/factory by the varying data (e.g. the sender operation and the operation(s) to inject, as in `Receiver(operation, [injected])`) instead of defining a separate subclass for each injection combination.
reason: Reduces boilerplate and duplication, and makes it trivial to add new recursion scenarios (direct, cyclical, etc.) without introducing a new subclass per operation.
common_pattern: Both generalizations state the same principle: in tests, replace per-case subclassing of helper/receiver objects with a single parameterized factory that takes the varying data (sender operation and injected operations) as arguments.

text: When creating a test fixture for dotfile-ignoring behavior, use a neutral dotfile name such as `.hidden` instead of `.gitignore`, and give the fixture contents a short explanatory message describing the behavior being tested (e.g., in `tests/view_tests/media/test/`, that the `directory_name()` view ignores files beginning with a dot).
reason: `.gitignore` has special meaning to Git and other tooling, which can obscure the purpose of the fixture; a neutral name plus self-documenting contents makes the test intent clear.
scope: test fixtures exercising dotfile/dot-prefix file ignoring behavior
common_pattern: Test fixtures that exercise dotfile-ignoring behavior should use a neutral dotfile name (e.g., `.hidden`) rather than a functionally-meaningful name like `.gitignore`, with contents that document the behavior under test.

text: When testing recursive signal/event handling (e.g., `post_operation` receivers under `tests/migrate_signals/`), write separate cases for direct recursion (a receiver re-emitting the operation it received) and cyclical/mutual recursion (a chain of receivers re-emitting each other), covering both apply and unapply paths where relevant. Use custom no-op operations rather than concrete migration operations like `CreateModel` so the recursion shape is isolated and easy to assert.
reason: Direct and cyclical recursion exercise different signal-emission and guard/error-handling paths, so testing only one topology leaves the other unverified; no-op operations keep these cases independent of real migration logic.
common_pattern: Testing recursive behavior: ensure explicit coverage of recursion topologies (direct vs cyclical) and turn recursion failures into clear, diagnosable assertions.

text: When a test exercises code that may recurse infinitely (e.g., cyclic references during render), wrap the recursion-prone assertion in `try/except RecursionError` and call `self.fail()` with a descriptive message naming the suspected cyclic reference.
reason: Turns an opaque `RecursionError` traceback into an explicit, human-readable test failure that points directly at the cyclic reference, improving debuggability.
common_pattern: Testing recursive behavior: ensure explicit coverage of recursion topologies (direct vs cyclical) and turn recursion failures into clear, diagnosable assertions.

text: When benchmarking or measuring elapsed time, ensure each measured iteration starts from a fresh state (e.g., recreate/reset iterators via the %timeit `setup` parameter) and use `time.perf_counter()` instead of `time.time()` for monotonic, high-resolution timing.
reason: %timeit reuses the same object across loops, so an exhausted iterator yields nothing after the first loop; and `time.perf_counter()` provides the highest available resolution and is monotonic, making elapsed-time measurements more accurate and stable than `time.time()`.
common_pattern: Accurate benchmarking and timing methodology: isolate measured state per iteration and use a high-resolution, monotonic clock for elapsed-time measurements.

text: When testing duration parsing/casting, cover both positive and negative durations. Use notation where a sign applies to the whole duration (e.g. '-MM:SS' maps to timedelta(minutes=-MM, seconds=-SS) and '-H:MM:SS' maps to timedelta(hours=-H, minutes=-MM, seconds=-SS)); do not assert component-level negative signs such as '4 -15:30'. Do not add negative-sign support to standard_duration_re without corresponding tests for those groups.
reason: A partially negative timedelta does not represent a negative duration string and can hide parser bugs; negative durations also exercise signed/unsigned representation paths (e.g. DurationField casts). Tests must not codify nonstandard notation as supported behavior.
scope: duration parser and DurationField cast tests (e.g. tests/utils_tests/test_dateparse.py, tests/db_functions/comparison/test_cast.py)
common_pattern: Duration parsing in Django's dateparse: correctness of negative-duration handling in tests, standards-compliant decimal separators, and accurate docstring documentation of supported formats.

text: When testing merge/union utilities, call the underlying merge function directly with simple primitive collections and structure each test case as `(list_of_input_lists, expected_result_list)`, consolidating all inputs into one list of lists instead of building full domain objects or separate nested per-case input/expected tuples.
reason: This isolates the merge/union algorithm, reduces setup boilerplate, and makes the expected merged/deduplicated/sorted result explicit in one test case.
scope: merge/union utility tests, especially list-merge tests such as `tests/forms_tests/tests/test_media.py`
common_pattern: Focused unit tests for merge/union utilities should call the underlying function directly with simple collections and use a consolidated input-list plus expected-result shape, rather than constructing full domain objects or separate per-case nested tuples.

text: Custom ExceptionReporter methods such as get_traceback_text must be covered by a debug-view test that hits the relevant endpoint and asserts the custom output; remove them if unused. For the text traceback path, issue an AJAX request (HTTP_X_REQUESTED_WITH='XMLHttpRequest') and assert the custom text with status_code=500.
reason: Prevents untested or dead custom exception-reporting code and ensures tests match the request path that actually produces the text traceback.
common_pattern: Testing custom exception reporter behavior: any custom ExceptionReporter override must be exercised through the debug-view endpoint, and the text traceback path specifically requires an AJAX request and a 500-response assertion.

text: In test helpers that capture environment variables, return a dictionary mapping variable names to values rather than a sorted list of 'NAME=VALUE' strings, and document the return in docstrings as a dict of the relevant variable family using wildcard notation (e.g., 'PG*') with '{}' for the empty case.
reason: Environment variables are order-insensitive, so sorting is unnecessary; a dict allows direct value access and avoids string parsing in tests. Documenting the dict return clarifies the data structure, uses correct wildcard notation, and specifies the empty mapping default.
scope: test helpers that capture environment variables
common_pattern: Test helpers should represent captured environment variables as a dictionary (not a sorted list of NAME=VALUE strings) and document that return type accordingly.

text: When testing inherited field attributes on models using multiple or abstract inheritance, derive the expected value from the derived class's MRO — the first class in the MRO that defines the field determines the inherited attributes — and cover both base-class orders (e.g., `ConcreteParent, AbstractParent` and `AbstractParent, ConcreteParent`), since C3 linearization can shadow a concrete field with an abstract one.
reason: Python resolves inherited attributes via the MRO; assuming declared base-class order or only testing one order can mask inheritance bugs or encode incorrect runtime expectations.
scope: tests for model inheritance / multiple inheritance
common_pattern: Accurately reflecting Django model inheritance semantics (MRO resolution, abstract/Meta inheritance, field extension hooks) in tests and documentation — deriving expectations from actual Python MRO behavior and documenting inheritance scope, rationale, and hooks instead of assuming intuitive base-class order or broad applicability.

text: In tests for `urlencode`, ensure `doseq=False` is covered with list/tuple inputs to prevent regression of the `and not doseq` branch, and avoid asserting on bytearray inputs with `doseq=False` as they represent an underspecified edge case.
reason: The `and not doseq` branch prevents expansion of list/tuple values; test coverage ensures it isn't accidentally removed. Bytearray inputs with `doseq=False` are a strange edge case with unsatisfying expected values, so such assertions should be removed rather than updated.
common_pattern: Testing the `doseq=False` behavior in Django's `urlencode` function

text: When testing `has_changed()` on array-backed form fields, cover distinct initial states (e.g. `field=None`, field omitted/default, and `field=[]`) rather than only empty collections, and keep tests to representative boundary cases instead of enumerating many positional permutations.
reason: Complementary testing generalizations (G11, G12) from PR#11970: one argues for broader coverage of distinct initial states, the other for trimming redundant permutations.
common_pattern: Conventions for implementing and overriding `has_changed()` (change detection) on Django form fields: normalize both sides via `to_python()`, respect `empty_values`/disabled semantics, extract shared normalization into a helper, and test the distinct initial-state boundaries.

text: When mocking a function's return value in tests, ensure the mock matches the real function's documented return type and container structure (e.g., an empty list for a list-returning function, a tuple for a documented triple).
reason: Mocks that use the wrong return type can hide bugs and break code relying on the real type's semantics (unpacking, indexing, type checks).
common_pattern: Test mocks should faithfully reproduce the real function's return values: both in type/structure and in explicit declaration for clarity.

text: When a mock return value would otherwise be built dynamically, declare it explicitly via literal expansion so the expected sequence is visible in the test.
reason: Explicitly declared return values keep tests straightforward and make expected data obvious to readers.
common_pattern: Test mocks should faithfully reproduce the real function's return values: both in type/structure and in explicit declaration for clarity.

text: Test foreign-key cache invalidation at the operation that actually triggers it: assert the cached related object after the `*_id` assignment, before `save()`, name such tests after the triggering operation (assignment vs. save), and add regression tests for no-op assignments (assigning the same FK ID should leave `is_cached()` true).
reason: Assertion timing and naming must match the behavior under test, otherwise a test can pass only because of persistence or be misleading about what invalidates the cache; and no-op assignments that unnecessarily clear the cache cause redundant queries, so they deserve an explicit regression guard.
common_pattern: Tests and comments must accurately reflect when and how foreign-key related-object caches are invalidated: test assertions should target the exact operation (assignment vs. save) that triggers invalidation, and inline comments should describe the current cache-clearing behavior rather than stale semantics.

text: Tests for URL safety checks (e.g., `http.is_safe_url`) should cover both `http://` and `https://` URLs with `secure=True` and with the default `secure=False`, so the secure flag's scheme enforcement is fully exercised.
reason: Security-sensitive URL validation can regress silently if only one scheme/flag combination is tested; covering both secure and non-secure schemes for each flag state ensures the `secure` parameter correctly enforces HTTPS-only behavior.
common_pattern: URL/scheme validation should be based on generic scheme parsing/membership rather than hard-coded protocol prefixes or partial allowlists, with tests covering both secure and non-secure scheme/flag combinations.

text: For cache-control patching tests, cover both boolean `no_cache=True` precedence over existing directives and string-valued `no_cache='...'` directive merging in the parameterized test table (e.g., in `test_patch_cache_control`).
reason: Ensures both pre-existing behavior and new feature behavior are verified consistently, and keeps new cases in a separate commit from the implementation patch.
common_pattern: Handling of HTTP Cache-Control `no_cache` semantics: which directives permit multiple values and what behaviors must be tested for the no_cache parameter.

text: When archive extraction is used for template scaffolding (e.g., startapp/startproject), handle permissions explicitly: apply permission-copying logic to both files and directories; if exact preservation is not required, OR read permission bits so extracted files/directories are at least readable/executable; and in tests account for the process umask (e.g., expect directory mode `0o777 & ~umask` or set a minimum permission mask when umask should not apply) and assert readability rather than exact permission-bit preservation.
reason: The extraction contract for templates is that generated files and directories are usable; exact original permission preservation is less important. Tests become environment-dependent unless they account for umask, and directory permissions are as important as file permissions.
common_pattern: Permission handling for archive extraction used in template scaffolding: implementation must apply permission logic to files and directories and ensure extracted content is readable/executable, while tests must account for the process umask and assert the readability contract rather than exact permission-bit preservation.

text: In test files that assert on serialized import paths, define enums and other classes at module level or as nested classes within TestCase classes, never inside test methods, to avoid `<locals>` segments in the serialized path. When fixing a bug in serialization/reflection of scoped classes, add a regression test that defines the class in the problematic scope (e.g., a nested enum inside a TestCase) and asserts the serialized path is correct.
reason: Serialized paths containing `<locals>` are brittle and depend on the exact test method scope, making assertions less stable and less representative of production usage. Regression tests in the problematic scope guarantee the fix addresses the exact scenario that triggered the bug and prevents future regressions.
common_pattern: Test organization for serialization/reflection of scoped classes: avoid defining classes inside test methods (which produce brittle `<locals>` paths) and add regression tests that reproduce the problematic scope.

text: When adding equality tests for expression or constructor objects, assert that equivalent normalized inputs compare equal (e.g., `Index('foo') == Index(F('foo'))`) and include a `pickle` or `deepcopy` roundtrip in addition to direct equality/inequality assertions.
reason: Equality should not depend on representation differences, object identity, or mutable internal state. Normalization equivalence tests and copy/serialization roundtrips catch regressions in equality semantics.
scope: tests for expressions and normalized model/index constructors
common_pattern: Testing equality semantics for expression/constructor objects so equality remains stable across input normalization and pickle/deepcopy roundtrips.

text: For client-side admin components that toggle UI state and persist it via localStorage, add QUnit tests in `js_tests` covering the toggle behavior and localStorage reads/writes, assuming localStorage works rather than mocking it.
reason: Provides regression coverage for state persistence and UI interactions while avoiding unnecessary mocking complexity.
scope: Django admin JavaScript testing (QUnit tests in `js_tests`)
common_pattern: Testing client-side admin UI state persistence in localStorage with QUnit, without mocking localStorage.

text: In schema tests, simulate model field initialization through the normal ORM paths: pass attributes such as `name=` directly to the field constructor instead of calling helpers like `set_attributes_from_name(...)` manually, and register dynamically added fields via `Model._meta.add_field(field)` before invoking schema_editor methods that resolve fields from model metadata.
reason: These are the same code paths the ORM uses when a model is defined, so the test faithfully reproduces real initialization and ensures schema_editor APIs (e.g., `add_index`) can find the field.
scope: schema tests / tests that mutate model schema
common_pattern: Simulating model initialization in schema tests by using the normal ORM construction/meta-registration paths rather than manual lower-level configuration, so tests faithfully mirror how a model is defined.

text: In tests that invoke the `flush` management command, pass the option name the command actually accepts (`skip_empty=True`), not `only_nonempty_tables=True`.
reason: Using a non-existent option name in the test call mismatches the command's real interface and breaks the test.
common_pattern: Both PRs touch the `flush` path: one about asserting the correct option name for the `flush` management command in tests, the other about how MySQL `sql_flush` decides which tables to clear. The shared surface is 'flush', but the underlying patterns are two distinct sub-patterns (test option naming vs. MySQL row-count gating). The MySQL sub-pattern (3 of 4 generalizations) is coherent and complementary: catalog row estimates are unreliable, so don't gate row removal on exact or approximate counts.

text: Tests for helpers that handle lazy objects (e.g., promises, lazy strings, `str`/`bytes`) must pass lazy objects — including as positional and keyword arguments — and assert those inputs are short-circuited/returned unchanged. Concretely-valued cases only exercise the underlying non-lazy code path and must not be the sole coverage.
reason: A helper whose purpose is to avoid prematurely evaluating lazy inputs can only be verified by a test that actually supplies a lazy value and asserts identity/equality/early-return; concrete-value tests silently validate only the underlying formatter.
common_pattern: Tests must exercise the lazy-evaluation code paths themselves, not just the concrete/eager equivalents — covering both how lazy inputs flow through helpers (rules 3 & 4) and how tests should respond when lazy-vs-eager evaluation timing changes (rules 1 & 2).

text: When the timing of an exception moves from lazy (iteration/query-compilation/evaluation time) to eager (method-call time), remove lazy-timing tests already covered by an eager-path test, and treat any newly-exposed exception from forced evaluation as a real latent bug to fix — do not revert the evaluation to keep the old test passing.
reason: Shifting error-raising earlier makes the old lazy test redundant, while any test that only passed because the lazy operation never ran is masking a defect that should be corrected rather than preserved.
common_pattern: Tests must exercise the lazy-evaluation code paths themselves, not just the concrete/eager equivalents — covering both how lazy inputs flow through helpers (rules 3 & 4) and how tests should respond when lazy-vs-eager evaluation timing changes (rules 1 & 2).

text: Before enabling an optional process-wide runtime/debugging feature such as faulthandler, guard the enable call with an is_enabled() check and the feature's enable flag, e.g. `if not faulthandler.is_enabled() and enable_faulthandler:`.
reason: Prevents redundant enabling, respects pre-existing process state, and avoids side effects from reconfiguring a facility that is already active.
common_pattern: Configuring process-wide diagnostics/debugging handlers (e.g., faulthandler) consistently and safely in parallel/multiprocessing test runners, including propagating enable/disable flags to worker processes and guarding enable calls against redundant activation.

text: When a helper's numeric formatting/parsing behavior depends on digit matching, add test cases using non-ASCII Unicode digits (e.g. full-width digits) so that an accidental narrowing of digit matching (such as switching `\d` to `[0-9]`) causes a test failure.
reason: Full-width Unicode digits match `\d` but not `[0-9]`; without such cases, assertions can pass even when digit-matching behavior is inadvertently narrowed, leaving the change undetected.
scope: global/testing — numeric parsing/formatting helpers whose behavior depends on which digits are matched
common_pattern: Project-wide regex convention: match digits with the explicit ASCII class `[0-9]` rather than `\d`, because `\d` matches Unicode decimal digits and produces surprising (non-canonical, non-normalized) behavior; tests must exercise the distinction.

text: Handle classmethods as class-level constructs: document them with the `classmethod` Sphinx directive (not `method`) and call them directly on the class under test rather than instantiating an object.
reason: Classmethods operate on the class itself, so using the correct directive ensures accurate rendered signatures, and calling them directly in tests avoids unnecessary object construction and makes the class-level contract explicit.
scope: Django testing tools docs and auth model tests
common_pattern: Classmethods should be treated as class-level constructs, not instance-level, in both documentation and tests.

text: Use `os.devnull` instead of hardcoding `'/dev/null'` whenever a null device path is needed, so tests remain portable across operating systems (e.g., Windows).
reason: The literal `/dev/null` is Unix-only and crashes on Windows; `os.devnull` resolves to the correct platform-specific device (`nul` on Windows).
common_pattern: Both generalizations state the same cross-platform testing rule: use `os.devnull` instead of hardcoding the POSIX path `'/dev/null'` so tests work on Windows too.

text: When writing tests for date-based generic views, choose dates/weeks that actually contain fixture objects, and assert computed week/date context values according to the week-start convention of the specific format directive under test.
reason: This prevents false-positive tests that return 404 instead of exercising lookup logic, and avoids encoding incorrect week semantics when different directives define weeks differently.
common_pattern: Tests for date-based generic views must keep test dates, fixture data, and date/week assertions semantically aligned: the chosen URL/date should exercise real object lookup, and expected computed date/week values must follow the specific format directive being tested.

text: When modifying tests for authentication or access-control behavior, first verify a known-good baseline: assert that authentication succeeds with the same credentials (and that behavior is confirmed across the relevant authentication states) before mutating user state or changing an existing assertion. If the behavior under test is not yet verified for all relevant auth states, revert the test change rather than commit a premature assertion update.
reason: Prevents false failures caused by credential typos or setup errors, isolates the mutated condition (e.g. inactive user, unauthenticated request) as the actual cause of the observed result, and avoids locking in assertions before the correct access-control behavior is established.
common_pattern: Both generalizations address validation of authentication-related test changes: before attributing an access-control outcome (404, auth failure) to the condition under test, establish a validated baseline (auth succeeds with the same credentials, behavior verified across auth states).

text: For auth validation/normalization changes, add integration tests that exercise the full public path — e.g., creating users through `AbstractUser`/model `clean()` and covering the `UserCreationForm` save/validation path — rather than only unit-testing validator helpers or mocking internal manager calls.
reason: Protects against regressions in model wiring and form behavior, directly exercises observable public APIs, and avoids coupling tests to internal implementation details.
common_pattern: Auth-related validation and normalization changes should be tested through the full public pipeline (model creation, clean(), form save/validation) rather than only unit-testing helper functions or mocking internal manager calls.

text: In introspection tests, target the exact metadata property under test: name helper functions after the specific metadata they return, and assert the exact metadata value affected by the bug across all relevant returned objects (not merely the presence or type of the object).
reason: Precise metadata-focused helpers and assertions make tests self-explanatory, reusable, and able to catch the specific regression being fixed.
scope: test helpers and introspection regression tests
common_pattern: Introspection tests should be explicit about the specific metadata property being examined, both in helper naming and in assertions.

text: Configure collation test fixtures with clearly named `test_collations` entries (referenced by name rather than by index/order) using canonical names — those returned by the backend's introspection queries (e.g. `utf8mb3_*` on MariaDB 10.6+) or portable ICU-style identifiers (e.g. `en-x-icu`) — rather than SQL aliases or OS/locale-specific names (e.g. `en_US`), and include a `'default'` entry so the default-collation path is covered.
reason: Named entries make test intent explicit and avoid coupling to dict ordering; introspection-returned names avoid mismatches with introspected metadata; ICU names are more reliably available across environments than OS/locale names; a `'default'` case exercises the most common code path.
common_pattern: Handling database collations correctly in Django tests and migration/schema operations: fixture configuration, test skipping, feature-flag modeling, and idempotency of collation DDL.

text: Add regression tests for structured error equality and representation: cover dict-based errors with different key orders and key mismatches, and construct expected ErrorList objects with the same error_class argument as the actual object so full string output is compared.
reason: Equality and representation semantics are subtle and easy to regress; tests should document whether field-key ordering, key sets, and error_class are significant.
common_pattern: Equality, hashing, and test assertions for structured error types must preserve all semantically meaningful structure — such as field-key mappings and error classes — rather than flattening to sorted messages or omitting class/type arguments.

text: Security fixes for SQL injection in query construction must add a regression test that reproduces the injection vector, covers malicious identifier payloads such as quotes, comment sequences, and boolean conditions, and asserts only the SQL fragment relevant to the injection vector rather than the entire generated SQL string.
reason: This captures the shared requirement across the cluster: regression tests are mandatory for SQL-injection fixes, must include malicious-input cases, and should stay focused on the injection behavior under test.
common_pattern: SQL injection regression testing for query construction and identifier interpolation: security fixes must include a regression test that reproduces the injection vector, exercises malicious payloads, and keeps assertions focused on the relevant SQL fragment.

text: When adding or modifying `get_or_create` default-update tests, include a separate multi-table inheritance (MTI) case using non-local concrete fields, and place it in `tests/get_or_create/tests.py` alongside the existing default-update tests.
reason: MTI with inherited concrete fields exercises different ORM field-resolution and default-update logic than local concrete fields; dedicated coverage prevents regressions and keeps related edge cases discoverable.
common_pattern: Django ORM test-model field design: choose test-only fields that match the behavior under test, using minimal non-concrete fields where full implementations are unnecessary, and adding dedicated coverage for MTI/non-local concrete field behavior in get_or_create default-update tests.

text: When adding a new hook, method, or wrapper that modifies or forwards context in a generic class-based view (e.g. `get_context_data()` or an `extra_context` parameter), add tests that exercise the hook/wrapper and assert the resulting context values. Keep such tests focused on the behavior under test: pass only the context needed (e.g. `{'extra_context': dict()}`) and supply concrete values only when the test asserts on them.
reason: Context-building hooks affect framework-level behavior and downstream subclassing; tests demonstrate intended behavior, verify context merging/forwarding order, and guard against regressions, while avoiding unnecessary dummy data keeps tests focused.
common_pattern: Testing changes to context-building behavior in class-based generic views: whenever a new hook, context modification, or `extra_context` forwarding is introduced, add tests that exercise the path and assert on the resulting context.

text: When modifying or testing cookie attribute handling (e.g., HttpResponse.set_cookie), add or update tests that assert both the parsed attribute value with assertEqual (e.g., c['name']['samesite'] == 'lax') and the serialized output contains the full directive with assertIn (e.g., 'SameSite=lax'), rather than only checking for the attribute name.
reason: This ensures the new type coercion or attribute-handling behavior is correct and protects against regressions; broad substring or name-only assertions can pass even when the attribute value or serialization is wrong.
common_pattern: Cookie attribute changes require tests that verify the actual parsed attribute value and the serialized directive, not merely that an attribute name appears.

text: Regression tests for upload error handling should simulate the actual failure condition (e.g., raising an exception on the closing boundary) rather than using an empty file, because empty files are ignored and do not exercise the intended error path.
reason: An empty file can be silently ignored, so the test will not raise `CustomUploadError` or call `upload_stopped()`, leaving the regression uncovered. This rule captures the need for faithful failure simulation in regression tests.
common_pattern: Best practices for writing and organizing file upload tests, covering both test reuse and error‑path fidelity.

text: In schema-editor tests that build a replacement field to compare against an existing one, carry over column-mapping arguments such as `db_column=old_field.column` so the new field targets the original database column.
reason: Without matching the column binding, the replacement field no longer represents the same underlying column and the no-op attribute comparison is not meaningful.
common_pattern: Django schema-alteration logic should derive per-field schema behavior from canonical, centralized Field metadata rather than ad-hoc/derived attribute inspection: (a) exclude non-DB-affecting attributes via an exhaustive, overridable list on Field, (b) test column existence with .concrete rather than .column, and (c) source DB-specific parameters from a db_params mapping.

text: When testing auth token invalidation on email change, include a test case using a model that overrides the email field (e.g., `CustomEmailField`, added to `tests/auth_tests/models/__init__.py`) in addition to the default `User` model, verifying tokens are invalidated when that custom email field changes.
reason: Token invalidation behavior depends on the specific email field name and how it is updated, so custom-email-field models exercise a path the default `User` model does not cover.
common_pattern: Auth token invalidation tests must cover models that override the email field (e.g., `CustomEmailField`), not just the default `User` model, because token invalidation depends on the specific email field name and how it is updated.

text: In `test_pickle_filteredrelation_m2m`, prefer conditions and setup values tied to the created model instance or explicit deterministic PKs over arbitrary literals such as `pk__lt=10` or an unused `added` date. For example, filter with `Q(m2mmodel=m2mmodel)` / `Q(m2mmodel__pk=m2mmodel.pk)` rather than assuming serial PK ordering, and use `id=1` instead of an unrelated date when the date value is not used.
reason: The test must remain valid on databases with non-serial/random primary keys, and unused arbitrary values make the test less clear and more database-dependent.
scope: test_pickle_filteredrelation_m2m; similar Django tests involving created model instances and PK assumptions
common_pattern: In `test_pickle_filteredrelation_m2m`, avoid arbitrary hardcoded values that assume serial primary-key behavior or rely on unused fields; instead reference the created model instance or use an explicit deterministic PK.

text: In tests/auth_tests/test_tokens.py, name test methods using `test_<method_under_test>_<scenario>`, using the exact API method under test (e.g., `check_token`, not a synonym like `verify`).
reason: Keeps the module uniform and makes tests easier to discover by clearly identifying the method under test and the covered behavior.
common_pattern: Conventions for tests in tests/auth_tests/test_tokens.py, dominated by a convergent test-method naming pattern, with a secondary sub-pattern about keeping tests focused on essential behavior rather than heavy bootstrap setup.

text: In tests/auth_tests/test_tokens.py, keep `DefaultTokenGeneratorTest` focused on asserting the essential behavior (e.g., that `SECRET_KEY` is lazily validated) rather than setting up a temporary project and subprocess bootstrap.
reason: The essential behavior under test is lazy validation, not the full interpreter/project bootstrap sequence; overly specific tests add unnecessary complexity.
common_pattern: Conventions for tests in tests/auth_tests/test_tokens.py, dominated by a convergent test-method naming pattern, with a secondary sub-pattern about keeping tests focused on essential behavior rather than heavy bootstrap setup.

text: When a change touches join-setup code (e.g., `setup_join`/`setup_joins`, aggregation transforms across relations), add a test that actually performs a JOIN followed by the transform, rather than only testing a transform on a direct, non-joined field.
reason: Modified join-setup paths are only exercised by queries that spawn a JOIN; a non-JOIN test can pass without covering the changed code, leaving join-related regressions undetected.
common_pattern: Both sub-patterns concern the `setup_join`/`setup_joins` code path: three generalizations demand that any change to join-setup logic be covered by a test that actually creates a JOIN, while a fourth addresses a state-mutation safety issue inside `setup_joins()` transform resolution. The dominant theme is 'treat join-setup code as a dedicated, explicitly-covered code path.'

text: For pytest-only toggles of global or process-wide flags, expose them via a fixture that sets the flag and restores the original value in a finally block, and represent the flag as a plain boolean variable (using global/nonlocal as needed) rather than a one-key dict.
reason: Fixtures with try/finally preserve test isolation and avoid expanding public configuration, while plain booleans communicate the intended state directly.
common_pattern: Managing test-only global/process-wide flags in pytest with proper isolation and clear state representation.

text: Assertions on string representations of database-generated timestamp/decimal values (e.g. `Now()` cast to text) must use a tolerant regex like `\d{1,precision}` rather than an exact digit count, accepting 1 through `connection.features.time_cast_precision` fractional digits, because backends such as PostgreSQL strip trailing zeros and vary formatting.
reason: Backends normalize numeric/text output differently (PostgreSQL strips trailing zeros), so exact-width assertions fail despite correct behavior.
scope: tests/db_functions/datetime/test_now.py and similar cross-backend timestamp assertions
common_pattern: Cross-database-backend fractional-second precision handling in Django's date/time pipeline: production typecast helpers must normalize sub-second values to Python's 6-digit microsecond limit, while tests asserting on string representations of database-generated timestamps must tolerate per-backend formatting variance (millisecond-only SQLite %f, PostgreSQL trailing-zero stripping).

text: Syntax-error test fixtures must use syntax that is unambiguously invalid in every supported Python version; do not rely on version-dependent constructs such as the walrus operator (`:=`).
reason: A fixture that is actually valid on some supported version will silently pass, causing the negative test to give false confidence.
common_pattern: Python version compatibility: code and tests must avoid syntax/constructs unavailable in the project's minimum supported Python version, with special care in negative test fixtures that must reliably trigger syntax errors.

text: In Django's test runner, after the overall result summary line (e.g., `FAILED (...)` or `OK`), print `Used shuffle seed: {seed} ({kind})` when shuffling is enabled.
reason: The final summary is the most visible output after a failed run; showing the exact seed there lets developers reproduce random-order failures without searching earlier logs.
common_pattern: Django test runner's shuffle feature: making the shuffle seed visible in final results and keeping shuffle-specific configuration logic encapsulated in the Shuffler class.

text: When building a test suite from labels that include failed-to-load modules, assert the exact test IDs included in the suite rather than only the number of tests.
reason: Counting tests can be insufficient to distinguish which modules contributed to the suite, potentially masking incorrect behavior.
common_pattern: Conventions for selecting, passing, and asserting test labels in Django test-runner tests and documentation: use stable and descriptive labels, follow local call conventions, and assert exact suite composition.

text: Test inherited behavior such as `__repr__` in the shared base test mixin (`BaseTests`) by instantiating `self.storage_class(request)` and asserting the expected class-qualname repr, so every storage subclass runs the same assertion instead of testing a single backend in isolation.
reason: Ensures inherited behavior is verified consistently across all subclasses and avoids repeating the same test per backend.
common_pattern: Shared behavior in class hierarchies should be defined once on the base class and verified once in the shared base test class, using the subclass attribute — rather than duplicated in each concrete implementation and its backend-specific test.

text: In tests/runtests.py, treat CLI labels that look like filesystem paths as test labels relative to RUNTESTS_DIR (not the current working directory): validate that the path exists and is under RUNTESTS_DIR with a descriptive error, resolve/normalize it (including trailing separators and dotted relative segments), and convert it to a dotted importable module name before passing it to the unittest loader. Add regression coverage for both trailing-slash and non-trailing-slash path forms, especially when invoked from outside tests/.
reason: This captures the shared behavior across the cluster: path labels such as `backends/postgresql` or `backends/postgresql/` should behave like dotted module labels such as `backends.postgresql`, work from any current directory, fail clearly when invalid, and not leak raw filesystem paths to unittest.
common_pattern: Path-style test labels passed to tests/runtests.py must be interpreted consistently from any working directory: resolve them relative to RUNTESTS_DIR, validate and normalize them, and convert them into dotted module names before unittest imports them. Regression tests should cover path-form variants such as trailing slashes.

text: When modifying Django ORM query construction logic in `django/db/models/sql/` (especially `query.py`, `split_exclude()`, and connector/negation splitting), add tests covering every affected branch and edge case—including connector/negation combinations, `allow_joins` values, model vs. no-model queries, and multi-join relation handling—and ensure the change does not introduce duplicate joins.
reason: Query construction and splitting logic is subtle and easy to get wrong; the cluster includes missed tests for connector/negation branches, untested `allow_joins` conditionals, and duplicate-join risks when modifying relation handling.
common_pattern: Modifications to Django ORM SQL query-construction logic in django/db/models/sql/ require comprehensive test coverage for affected branches and edge cases, and careful handling of joins/relations.

text: Do not write tests that assert performance characteristics without actually measuring them (e.g., 'does not take forever'). Either include a real timing/timeout check so the test is meaningful, or omit the test. Conversely, do not require tests for code paths that are purely performance optimizations and don't affect correctness behavior.
reason: Without measurement, performance-intent tests pass regardless of regressions and provide no value, while requiring tests for optimization-only code adds maintenance burden without verifying the correctness contract.
common_pattern: Tests should only exist where they verify meaningful behavior; performance-related claims require actual measurement, and optimization-only code paths that don't affect correctness don't need test coverage.

text: In test helper modules, parameterize shared request-building helpers with the request class variant and let the helper apply setting-specific branches; custom test request classes should accept per-class configuration via class attributes rather than __init__ arguments.
reason: Merged complementary halves from the same review comment: parameterizing helpers with a request class argument lets the helper handle setting-specific branches, while using class attributes for per-class configuration avoids custom constructors and keeps helper-based request construction uniform.
common_pattern: Test helper and test client APIs should be designed for consistency, parameterization, and class-attribute-based configuration to avoid duplication and reduce bugs.

text: In sitemap response tests, assert the presence or absence of the `Last-Modified` header according to whether the sitemap has `lastmod` data (present for full sitemaps, absent for partial sitemaps) rather than relying only on XML body assertions.
reason: Header assertions directly verify Django sitemap `lastmod` semantics and expose the behavioral difference between partial and full sitemap cases.
common_pattern: This cluster is thematically tied to conventions for Django sitemap test fixtures and test cases (tests/sitemaps_tests/), but it actually contains several distinct sub-patterns: (1) test documentation via docstrings, (2) precise naming of sitemap URL fixtures, and (3) header-level assertions for lastmod semantics. Only the docstring convention has clear multi-PR support; the other sub-patterns are single-PR but represent concrete, reusable conventions.

text: In tests, be aware of Windows filename restrictions: sanitization/path-handling test suites should explicitly include cases for reserved characters (`><:?|*`) and names ending in a period or space, while unrelated test fixtures should use plain alphabetic names like 'nonexistent' instead of names containing special characters or trailing dots (e.g. '...'), because such names behave differently or are invalid on Windows and break cross-platform test runs.
reason: Underlying filesystems may permit these names, but the Windows shell and UI do not; therefore tests validating sanitization must cover them, while ordinary test fixtures must avoid them so the suite runs reliably on both POSIX and Windows.
common_pattern: Awareness of Windows filesystem filename restrictions (reserved characters, trailing dots/spaces) when writing tests — using such names deliberately only when testing sanitization, and avoiding them elsewhere to keep tests cross-platform.

text: When changing how expression state flags like `is_summary` are set, add a regression test covering the case where an aggregate with `default` is used in a non-summary context.
reason: Ensures the flag is only set in summary contexts and prevents regressions in query construction.
common_pattern: When wrapping an existing ORM expression in a derived expression, propagate metadata flags (notably `is_summary`) from the wrapped expression or the surrounding summary context instead of hardcoding them; this is required for correctness in annotations and subqueries, and should be covered by regression tests.

text: Keep source-map comment/URL coverage in the dedicated staticfiles source-map test suite and fixtures (e.g., source_map.js, source_map.css) rather than generic module fixtures; when modifying source-map parsing/rewriting regexes, add representative examples to the corresponding fixture — including data: URI cases — so the changed behavior is tested.
reason: The motivations show two complementary halves: (1) source-map tests and fixtures belong in the dedicated source-map locations (existing staticfiles test suite / source_map.js / source_map.css), not mixed into generic module fixtures; and (2) regex changes for source-map handling require fixture-based coverage, especially for edge cases like data: URIs, which are easy to regress. Both halves serve the same principle: source-map-specific behavior is tested in source-map-specific places with representative inputs.
